01-001.r: Seven fundamental physical quantities: length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, luminous intensity, amount of substance. Force, velocity and work are not among them.
01-001.h: LMT + CTL + A: Length, Mass, Time; Current, Temperature, Luminous intensity; Amount of substance.

01-002.r: Power = work ÷ time (rate of doing work); SI unit watt = joule per second; also written in kilowatt (kW).

01-003.r: Electric power → watt. Ampere → electric current; volt → electric potential; coulomb → electric charge.
01-003.t: Don't confuse watt (power) with volt (potential difference).

01-004.r: Force = mass × acceleration; SI unit newton (kg·m/s²); modern definition from Isaac Newton's laws of motion.

01-005.r: Work = force × displacement in the direction of force (a scalar); SI unit joule (= newton metre), also the unit of energy.

01-006.r: Frequency → hertz (Hz), the derived SI unit = one cycle per second.

01-008.r: Processor speed → hertz/gigahertz: clock cycles completed per second; 1 GHz = 1 billion cycles per second.

01-009.r: GHz (gigahertz = one billion hertz) on a computer indicates its speed: the clock or processing speed of the central processor.

01-010.r: Resistivity ρ = RA/l; its SI unit is ohm-metre (Ωm). 'Ohm-metre' is the unit of resistivity.
01-010.c: None of the options is ohm-metre, the unit of resistivity; (d) ohm is the unit of resistance. Also, capacitance is measured in farads; the faraday is a quantity of charge, not that unit.

01-012.r: Magnetic field B (magnetic flux density) → SI unit tesla.

01-013.r: 1 tesla = 1 weber per square metre (Wb/m²) = 1 newton per ampere-metre; named after Nikola Tesla.

01-014.r: Not matched: radioactivity – curie (old non-SI unit); SI unit is becquerel (Bq). Lens power – dioptre, pressure – pascal, heat – joule are correct.

01-015.r: Light-year → unit of distance: the distance light travels in one year ≈ 9.461 trillion km.
01-015.t: A light-year measures distance, not time or speed.

01-018.r: Astronomical distances use light-years because the speed of light in vacuum is always the same (not even affected by gravity).

01-019.r: 1 parsec = distance at which Earth's mean orbital radius subtends 1 arc second (parallax) ≈ 3.262 light-years ≈ 206265 AU ≈ 30.9 trillion km.
01-019.h: PAR-SEC = PARallax of one arc SECond.

01-020.r: Parsec is a unit of distance: 1 parsec ≈ 3.262 light-years; nearest option 3.25 light-years.

01-022.r: 1 centimetre = 0.39 inch → multiply centimetres by 0.39 to get inches.

01-023.r: 1 foot = 0.305 m = 30.5 × 10⁷ nm → six feet ≈ 183 × 10⁷ nm (1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m).

01-026.r: Ampere → SI unit of electric current; 1 ampere means about 6.25 quintillion electrons flowing per second.

01-027.r: Megawatt → unit of power generated (in power stations/plants); 1 MW = 1 million watt.

01-028.r: Acceleration → metre/second² (m/s²); force → newton; work done → joule; impulse → newton second (Ns).

01-029.r: Not matched: pressure – dyne. SI unit of pressure is pascal; dyne is the CGS unit of force. Work – joule, force – newton, mass – kg are correct.

01-030.r: Watt → power; knot → speed of a ship; nautical mile → navigation (distance at sea); calorie → heat.

01-031.r: Joule → work; ampere → current; watt → power; volt → electric potential.

01-032.r: 1 horsepower = 746 watt (horsepower is a unit of power; 1 watt = 1 joule/second).

01-033.r: Not matched: light-year is a unit of distance, not time. Knot → ship speed; nautical mile → navigation distance; angstrom → wavelength of light.

01-034.r: Angstrom (Å) → length unit for wavelengths of electromagnetic waves; 1 Å = 10⁻¹⁰ m = 0.1 nm; named after Swedish physicist Anders Jonas Angstrom.

01-035.r: Mach → high speed (Mach 1 = speed of sound); angstrom → wavelength; pascal → pressure; joule → energy.

01-039.r: Not matched: Celsius is a temperature scale, not a heat unit (heat → calorie). 1 hp = 746 W; 1 nautical mile = 1.852 km; decibel → sound intensity.

01-040.r: Watt is a unit of power, not heat; calorie, kilocalorie and kilojoule are units of heat.

01-041.r: Centigrade is a temperature scale, not a heat unit; calorie, erg and joule are units of heat energy.
01-041.t: Don't confuse heat (energy: joule, calorie, erg) with temperature (Centigrade, Fahrenheit, Kelvin scales).

01-042.r: 1 km = 1000 m; 1 m = 100 cm (SI unit of distance is metre).

01-043.r: 1 pikogram (picogram) = 10⁻¹² g. Milligram 10⁻³, microgram 10⁻⁶, nanogram 10⁻⁹, femtogram 10⁻¹⁵ gram.

01-044.r: Pascal (Pa) → SI unit of pressure or stress = 1 newton per square metre (N/m²); named after Blaise Pascal.

01-046.r: The unit kg/cm² is not a correct pressure unit; the proper (deprecated) form is kgf/cm² (1 kgf/cm² = 98,066.5 Pa), so the answer is 'None of the above'.

01-047.r: Bar, pascal (Pa), torr and atmosphere (atm) are all units of pressure; pascal (1 N/m²) is the SI unit.

01-048.r: Bar → metric (not SI) unit of pressure, used for atmospheric pressure; 1 bar = one lakh (hundred thousand) pascal.

01-050.r: Strain (change in shape or size, a ratio) is dimensionless and has no unit; stress and pressure → pascal; force → newton.

01-051.r: 1 barrel of oil ≈ 159 litres (158.9873 L) = 42 US gallons.

01-052.r: Smallest is fermi (femtometre) 10⁻¹⁵ m; angstrom 10⁻¹⁰ m, nanometre 10⁻⁹ m, micron 10⁻⁶ m.

01-053.r: Cusec (cubic feet per second) → rate of water flow; byte (eight bits) → computer; Richter → earthquake intensity; bar → pressure.

01-055.r: NTU (nephelometric turbidity unit) → turbidity of water, i.e. its opaqueness due to suspended solids.

01-056.r: Solar constant (solar energy received per unit area at one astronomical unit from the Sun) ≈ 1.4 kW/m².

01-057.r: Ozone layer thickness → Dobson unit (DU); 1 DU = 0.01 mm thickness at STP; named after G.M.B. Dobson.

02-001.r: SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) → locates submerged objects (submarines, icebergs) by sending ultrasonic pulses and receiving their echo.

02-002.r: SONAR is mostly used by navigators; it works with ultrasonic waves.

02-004.r: Audiometer → intensity of sound; anemometer → wind speed and force; chronometer → exact time (longitude at sea); audiophone → small hearing aid.

02-008.r: Not matched: tacheometer – a theodolite that measures distance to a target, not pressure difference. Anemometer → wind speed; ammeter → current; pyrometer → high temperature.

02-010.r: Not matched: galvanometer measures small electric current (coil deflection), not resistance. Voltmeter → potential difference; ammeter → current; potentiometer → EMF.

02-011.r: Pyrometer (radiation thermometer) → very high temperature, even of distant objects like the Sun; based on Stefan–Boltzmann law (E ∝ T⁴).

02-014.r: Total radiation pyrometer → very high temperatures like 2000°C, by measuring thermal radiation without touching the object.

02-016.r: Pyrheliometer → solar radiation (the other device for solar radiation: pyranometer).

02-017.r: Manometer → uses a liquid column to measure pressure of gases (and liquids).

02-018.r: Ammeter → electric current; hygrometer → relative humidity; spring balance → weight; barometer → atmospheric pressure.

02-019.r: Not matched: ammeter measures electric current, not power. Odometer → distance by vehicle wheels; ondometer → frequency of EM waves; audiometer → sound intensity.

02-020.r: Odometer → distance travelled by a vehicle; speedometer → speed; chronometer → precise time (longitude at sea); ammeter → current.

02-021.r: Barometer → atmospheric pressure; a sudden fall of mercury in it indicates a thunderstorm.

02-022.r: Simple barometer → long glass tube filled with mercury, turned upside down into a mercury container (other types: water, oil, aneroid).

02-023.r: Lactometer → density of milk; butyrometer → fat content of milk.
02-023.t: Don't confuse lactometer (milk density) with butyrometer (milk fat).

02-025.r: Hygrometer → relative humidity; hydrometer → relative density of liquids; lactometer → milk density; potentiometer → electric potential.
02-025.t: Don't confuse hygrometer (humidity) with hydrometer (density of liquids).

02-026.r: Hygrometer → humidity (moisture) in air; spectrometer → properties of light; eudiometer → change in volume of a gas mixture.

02-029.r: Hygrometer → humidity; pyrometer → high temperature; hypsometer → height or altitude; thermostat → keeps temperature near a set point.

02-030.r: Ringelmann Scale → density (opacity) of smoke; devised by French professor Maximilien Ringelmann in 1888.

02-031.r: Thermoresistor → works as an electronic thermometer: its resistance changes with temperature.

02-032.r: EEG (electroencephalogram) → records electrical activity of the brain through electrodes on the scalp.

02-033.r: Stethoscope → heart sound; sphygmomanometer → blood pressure; caratometer → purity of gold; luxmeter → intensity of light.

02-036.r: RADAR (Radio Detection and Ranging) → detects presence, range, angle and velocity of objects (aircraft, ships, weather) using radio waves.
02-036.t: RADAR uses radio waves, not light or sound waves.

02-037.r: Richter scale (Charles F. Richter, 1935) → magnitude of an earthquake (energy released; amplitude of seismic waves).

02-040.r: Not matched: Richter scale – humidity; it rates earthquake magnitude. Celsius → temperature; kilowatt hour → electricity; Rh factor → blood.

02-041.r: Seismograph → records seismic waves of earthquakes; crescograph (J.C. Bose) → plant growth; Geiger counter → radioactivity; raingauge → rain.

02-045.r: Earthquake → seismograph; height → altimeter; electric current → ammeter; resistance → ohm.

02-046.r: Fathometer → depth of sea (ultrasonic waves); barometer → atmospheric pressure; hygrometer → humidity; altimeter → height.

02-048.r: Anemometer → wind velocity; seismograph → earthquakes; barograph → atmospheric pressure; hygrometer → humidity.

02-049.r: Not matched: seismometer – it measures earthquake seismic waves, not curvature of surface. Manometer → pressure; carburettor → IC engine; cardiograph → heart movement.

02-050.r: Phonometer → tests the force of the human voice; photometer → intensity of light.
02-050.c: The book gives no single answer (*): none of the four options describes a phonometer.

02-051.r: Polygraph (lie detector) → records blood pressure, pulse, respiration and skin conductivity while a person answers questions.

02-052.r: Theodolite → measures angles in the horizontal (azimuth) and vertical (elevation) planes.

02-053.r: Accelerometer is needed in all three: airbag deployment on crash, laptop free-fall hard-drive shut-off, and phone tilt rotating the display.
